lines.text: In December 1900, three lighthouse keepers vanished from a tiny Scottish island.
The Flannan Isles lighthouse sits off the west coast of Scotland, in the Outer Hebrides.
When the relief ship arrived on December 26th, nobody came to meet it.
The gate and door were shut. The beds were unmade. The clocks had stopped.
The lamps were cleaned and ready. And one man's coat was still on its peg.
James Ducat, Thomas Marshall and Donald McArthur were never found.
Creepy log entries about storms and prayers went viral later. Researchers found they were invented.
The investigator at the time believed a giant wave swept them off the rocks.
But why would all three leave the lighthouse at once?

sources.claim: Last believed on duty around 15 December 1900; relief ship Hesperus arrived 26 December; door shut, beds unmade, clocks stopped, lamps ready, McArthur's coat on its peg
Keepers James Ducat, Thomas Marshall, Donald McArthur never found; dramatic logbook entries were later fictions (Mike Dash); Robert Muirhead concluded a large wave swept them away

publish.title: Three Lighthouse Keepers Vanished Without a Trace 🌊
publish.description: Flannan Isles, 1900. Stopped clocks, an unmade bed, a coat on its peg, and three men who were never seen again.
